confirmed.why_suspicious: Norm Reeves is a large real US Honda/Toyota dealership group — a car dealer running a Binance-branded search ad. Viewed creative: display URL www.binance.com/, headline 'Binance - Binance Are Trust By Our User', body 'Binance Register Now Get Your Free Binance Account Today! Signup Take Less Than 40 Seconds'. The ungrammatical headline ('Are Trust By Our User') is machine-written scam copy, and the two-day flight (2025-09-07 to 2025-09-08) is a burn-and-drop pattern. Fits either a hijacked/rented verified ad account or a throwaway entity in a Binance-affiliate farm. Advertiser-mode pull blocked by the 302.

verdict.reasoning:
CORE CLAIM SURVIVES — but its stated evidence is partly false and its label is imprecise. Positive control PASSED in the same session (domain trezor.io US -> 40 creatives, Trezor Company s.r.o., AR07426507167890407425), so these results are trustworthy.

WHAT REFUTATION ATTEMPTS FOUND:
1. Name-coincidence check (the "trezor = safe in Czech" trap) FAILS to refute. "Norm Reeves, Inc." is a real California corporation d/b/a Norm Reeves Honda Superstore (FTC C-4436 / 132-3151). Not an unrelated business sharing a name.
2. The claim's own excuse — "advertiser-mode pull blocked by the 302" — is FALSE. Routed via the residential exit (scratchpad/atcprox.py), atc.search_by_advertiser("AR13216877914810744833","US") returns 58 creatives across 2 pages. This is the decisive evidence the claimant never got, and it strengthens the claim.
3. Advertiser history: 49 of 58 creatives run 2023-04-20 -> 2025-09-07 for normreeveshondacerritos.com — Honda CR-V/Civic inventory ads, Honda logo, Google Business Profile local ads ("Honda dealer · Cerritos", 4.4 stars, 6,132 reviews). Genuinely the dealership's own live account.
4. Overlap test kills the innocent "dormant account resold" reading: the Binance search ad (CR08298723010328657921) starts 2025-09-07 04:31:54 UTC while ALL 49 Honda creatives are still serving (last-shown up to 2025-09-07 21:04) — 16.5h overlap. Intrusion into a LIVE account.
5. Nine crypto-era creatives: 1 Binance search text ad + 8 contentless cloaked display creatives on 2025-09-08 ("To continue - click here" / "Click Here to Continue" / "Open" over generic stock photos, no brand, no product). Neither a Honda dealer nor a legitimate Binance affiliate produces those.
6. Account is dark after 2025-09-08 20:36:58 — zero creatives in 11 months. Consistent with Google suspending a compromised account.

CORRECTIONS REQUIRED BEFORE PUBLICATION:
a) "IMPERSONATOR" is the wrong label. Display URL and site name are binance.com; nothing impersonates Trezor and no phishing destination is evidenced. The party impersonated is Norm Reeves, whose verified advertiser identity was used without authorisation. Using "impersonator" inside a seed-phrase-phishing teardown implies consumer phishing that was not measured.
b) "Throwaway entity in a Binance-affiliate farm" is REFUTED as an alternative — it is a 2.5-year real dealer account. Presenting it as equal-weight understates the finding.
c) The bad-grammar argument is unsafe alone: "Get Your Free Binance Account Today! Signup Take Less Than 40 Seconds" appears verbatim across at least 5 unrelated binance.com advertisers (Floral Garden, 24 De Nails Ltd, AMERICA GLOBAL CARS LLC, Pham Huy Minh). It identifies the operator's shared template pool, not the account's status. "Machine-written" is unsupported.
d) The 2-day flight is only meaningful in contrast to the 2.5-year legit history; standing alone it is weak (VISA EUROPE LTD ran 3 days, AMERICA GLOBAL CARS LLC ran a month).
e) Do NOT generalise the cohort. Tested: VISA EUROPE LTD (AR02700591065387237377, 4 creatives all first-shown 2025-09-29) and AMERICA GLOBAL CARS LLC (AR09639302837372452865, 1 creative) are crypto-only shells with no prior history. Norm Reeves is the ONLY hijacked-real-business in the set of 11 binance.com US advertisers.
f) NO link to the Trezor campaign is established: Sept 2025 vs Aug 2026, Binance vs Trezor, no shared infrastructure. Including it in the Trezor teardown asserts a connection that does not exist.

UNMEASURED: ATC exposes no final/landing URL and the ads are 11 months dead, so the destination of the 8 cloaked creatives — where actual harm would live — is unknown. The inference that the Binance ad landed on real binance.com rests on Google's display-URL policy, not on a measurement.

AR13216877914810744833 "NORM REEVES INC" is the genuine Google Ads account of Norm Reeves Honda Superstore Cerritos (real California corporation, FTC C-4436), which ran 49 normreeveshondacerritos.com Honda inventory and local ads continuously from 2023-04-20. On 2025-09-07 04:31 UTC — while all 49 dealer ads were still serving — an intruder began running a Binance brand-bidding search ad (display URL www.binance.com/, shared affiliate-farm copy template) from the same account, followed on 2025-09-08 by 8 contentless cloaked display creatives ("To continue - click here" over stock photos). All dealer ads stop 2025-09-07 21:04; everything stops 2025-09-08 20:36 and the account has been dark for 11 months — a ~40-hour takeover window ended by account suspension. verdict.reasoning:
CORE ALLEGATION CONFIRMED, NOT REFUTED — but the claim contains one fatal error that must be struck before publication.

VERIFICATION METHOD: urllib and plain curl both hit 429 / Google /sorry/ from this box. Used the existing in-repo shim scripts/vf_atc.py (curl + Gonzo residential exit), atc.py payloads unchanged. POSITIVE CONTROL PASSED ON EVERY RUN, bracketing each key query: trezor.io US = 40 creatives, "Trezor Company s.r.o.", AR07426507167890407425.

WHAT I CONFIRMED:
- Advertiser AR10173951224055857153 exists: display name "Crypto recovery" (field 22 also "Crypto recovery"), verified domain walletrecovery.click, 3 creatives in ES, fully paginated (no cursor — not truncated).
- Rendered creatives match the claimed copy VERBATIM: '¿PROBLEMAS CRIPTO? ¡SOLUCIONAMOS TODO!', headline '¿Fondos Digitales Atrapados?', body 'Recuperación fondos urgente. Equipo español legal+técnico. Resultados comprobados.', advertiser shown as 'Wallet Recovery' on walletrecovery.click. (Claim listed 4 tickboxes; there are actually 5 visible + 1 cropped — under-listed, not fabricated.)
- ES-ONLY established far more strongly than the claim did. I pulled LookupService/GetCreativeById, which returns a per-region reach breakdown: all three creatives list exactly ONE geo entry, 2724 = ES, ~20,000–27,000 impressions, 20251111→20251120. Plus a 20-region advertiser sweep (US GB DE FR NL MX AR CL CO PT IT BE CH IE BR CA AT PL CZ RO) = all zero with a passing control at the end of the same run.
- NOT brand impersonation: zero occurrences of trezor/ledger/metamask/exodus/coinbase/binance in the ads or the live site. The "trezor = safe/vault in Czech" false-positive test is inapplicable — the word never appears.

NEW EVIDENCE THE CLAIM DID NOT HAVE (makes fraud much harder to argue against):
- Second creative CR06623445384159035393: "Expertos españoles recuperación digital. +62M recuperados. 98% éxito. Consulta gratis." — quantified success-rate guarantee.
- RDAP: domain registered 2025-11-04 (Hostinger/Tucows), registrant redacted. urlscan capture from 2025-11-04 shows a bare WordPress "Hello world!" install. First ad served 7 days later. The live site claims "2016 Founded", "© 2016–2025", "3 Global Offices", "50+ Experts".
- Live site sells "Private Key Restoration / Seed Phrase Recovery / Hardware Wallet Access" and claims "ESTD Licensed" and "MiCA Compliant". ESTD is not a licensing body (it is the abbreviation for "established"); MiCA authorises crypto-asset service providers and does not license fund-recovery firms. Both credentials fabricated.
- Intake form harvests "Amount Lost", "Deposit Method", "Name or Domain of Fraudulent Company" — textbook advance-fee re-victimisation funnel. Contact = UK mobile +447448408419, Telegram @walletrecovery, WhatsApp. NO UK company named "Wallet Recovery" exists at Companies House despite the claimed London office.
- Ad says "Equipo español" but the landing page is entirely in English with London/Munich/Rome offices and no Spanish entity named.
- Two creative variants are visibly AI-generated garbage: "Wallet & Exchange Recery" and "¿Enalimś fado? yllo covery Rate? Crypto foreIfly Recoverwite?" — unattended disposable creative.
- Alternate-hypothesis test done: a legitimate long-established operator in this niche DOES exist (walletrecoveryservices.com, 12+ yr domain, genuine Trustpilot record). walletrecovery.click is not it and does not claim to be. No legitimate-namesake explanation available.

THREE CORRECTIONS REQUIRED BEFORE PUBLICATION:
1. FATAL — the Trezor linkage is temporally impossible and must be STRUCK. The claim says this is "secondary victimisation of exactly the population this Trezor campaign created". The ads ran 2025-11-11 → 2025-11-21; the Trezor Google Sites drains were 2026-08-05/07, EIGHT MONTHS AND FIFTEEN DAYS LATER. It cannot have targeted victims of an incident that had not yet occurred. This was the entire reason the item sat in a Trezor report, and it collapses. The finding is real but belongs in a different document.
2. "running ads in region ES" is false in tense — last served 2025-11-21, 261 days before today. I validated the date field with a control: legitimate Trezor's latest last_shown is 2026-08-09 (today), so the field is live and the staleness is genuine, not an artifact.
3. "Recovering a LOST PRIVATE KEY is cryptographically impossible" is over-broad as written and a knowledgeable reader would refute it — forgotten-password and partial-seed brute-force recovery is a real legitimate niche. Defensible rewrite: no honest operator advertises a 98% success rate or blanket "any lost private key recovered", and tracing funds is not retrieving them.

Accurate as stated: the 10-day burst (9.7 days; per-region data 20251111→20251120), the throwaway .click TLD, the generic "Crypto recovery" account name, Spanish-language and Spain-targeted.

Setting refuted=false because I am not uncertain: rendered creatives, a live landing page with fabricated licensing and founding date, a 7-day-old domain, and in-payload ATC reach data all independently confirm a fraudulent advance-fee recovery operation. But the item must not be published in the Trezor report in its current form.
verdict.real_nature: A genuine advance-fee crypto "fund recovery" scam funnel — but an ENDED, Spain-only display campaign with no connection to the Trezor incident. Advertiser AR10173951224055857153 ("Crypto recovery" / displayed as "Wallet Recovery"), verified domain walletrecovery.click, 3 creatives, geo 2724 (ES) exclusively, ~20-27k impressions, served 2025-11-11 to 2025-11-21 only — 8.5 months BEFORE the Trezor Google Sites drains, so it cannot be secondary victimisation of that campaign's victims. Not an impersonator of Trezor or any brand (no brand string appears anywhere) and not a legitimate namesake business: domain registered 2025-11-04 as a bare WordPress install, first ad 7 days later, while the site claims "2016 Founded", "$62M+ Recovered", "98% Success Rate", "Trusted by 15,000+ Clients", "ESTD Licensed" and "MiCA Compliant" (both fabricated credentials — ESTD is not a regulator; MiCA does not license recovery firms). Sells the impossible ("Private Key Restoration", "Seed Phrase Recovery"), harvests "Amount Lost" / "Deposit Method" / "Name or Domain of Fraudulent Company" via a lead form, contacts victims through a UK mobile, Telegram and WhatsApp, and has no company registration at Companies House despite claiming a London office. Ad copy is Spanish ("Equipo español") while the landing page is English-only — a geo-targeted re-victimisation funnel aimed at already-defrauded Spanish crypto holders generally, not at Trezor victims.

**One survivor, and it is not an impersonator:** `NORM REEVES INC` **`AR13216877914810744833`** (US) — the genuine Norm Reeves Honda Cerritos account, 49 dealer creatives running continuously since 2023‑04‑20, **intruded on 2025‑09‑07 04:31 UTC with 16.5 h of overlap with live dealer ads**, then 1 Binance brand‑bid search ad + **8 contentless cloaked display creatives** ("To continue – click here"), dark since 2025‑09‑08 20:36. That is a **confirmed ad‑account takeover**, Binance‑branded, **11 months before** the Trezor incident, no phishing destination evidenced, no shared infrastructure. Do not file it under Trezor.

Also worth stating explicitly, because it looks damning and is not: the three non‑owner advertisers returned by `trezor.io` domain searches — `JAI MATA DI ENTERPRISES` **`AR12256293412315070465`**, `CÔNG TY TNHH NỘI THẤT PHI TUẤN` **`AR14125311996685451265`**, `Willing Media Co., Limited` **`AR06640749188919328769`** (seen in FR, CZ, PL, IN, IE, TR, JP, KR) — render, when the creative PNG is actually downloaded, as: a **`affil.trezor.io`** ad (Trezor's own affiliate subdomain), a **Bybit `www.bybit.eu`** ad, and a **MEXC `www.mexc.com`** ad respectively. ## 3. Clusters whose positive control FAILED

**No delivered cluster's negatives rest on a control that was failing at collection time.** Controls that passed: US 40 (166 paginated), GB 40/40, IE 40/40, FR 40, BE 40, CZ 195, PL 104, ES 40 ×4, IT 40 ×4, CA 40/40, JP 4 (owner present). Four caveats that must be stated in the report:

- **US — partial blackout, 4 named gaps.** After ~70 calls the endpoint went HTTP 302 for 25+ minutes. Advertiser‑mode enrichment for `VISA EUROPE LTD`, `NORM REEVES INC`, `AMERICA GLOBAL CARS LLC` (`AR09639302837372452865`) and `YUHUA TRADING AND CONSTRUCTION` (`AR00456213985981628417`) was cut off — **unverified‑blocked, not absent**. (Three were later completed by the verifiers.)
- **Runs that did fail and were superseded — their output is worthless and must not be cited:** `advdetail.json` CA leg (control_before *and* control_after = HTTP 302), `sweep_ca_au.json` AU control_after = HTTP 302, `sweep_IN.json` US control = HTTP 500 both ends. Superseded by `advdetail_CA.json` (40/40), `au_gap.json` (10/10), `reverify_hosting.json` (100/100).
- **Regions where an in‑region positive control is structurally impossible — Trezor does not advertise there:** **SG** (`trezor.io` SG = 0), **KR** (=1, and it is PHI TUẤN's Bybit ad, not Trezor), **TR** (=2, PHI TUẤN only), **IN** (=3, PHI TUẤN + Willing Media, zero Trezor), **VN** (=0). | Trezor Uspomena | `AR17076931539608010753` | RS |

Safe/vault domains in the same index: `trezory.cz`, `trezory24.cz`, `aaa-trezory.cz`, `novetrezory.cz`, `trezorstore.cz`, `trezormaster.cz`, `trezorynazbrane.cz`, `trezory-celakovice.cz`, `justratrezory.cz`, `otevrenitrezoru.cz`, `trezor.sk`, `rottner-trezory.sk`, `rottner-trezorji.si`, `trezorbhp.pl`, `trezor.shop`, `hotel-trezor.de`, `correcttrezor.hu`, `petrik-trezor.hu`. Only `AR07426507167890407425` **Trezor Company s.r.o. (CZ)** is the wallet brand.

## 5. The single most defensible conclusion

**ATC holds no record of this attack, and its "domain" field cannot be used to accuse or clear anyone.**

Two halves, both measured:

- **What it does not record.** Across 18 regions with a passing control, `sites.google.com` and every other Google‑owned hosting domain return **zero** advertisers, while `trezor.io` simultaneously returns the real Trezor (40–166 creatives). The attacker, the creative and the campaign are absent — a **true negative, not a broken query**. The mechanism is structural: ATC drops creatives when an account is terminated for policy violation, so the archive is emptiest exactly where enforcement worked. ATC is therefore useless as a forensic source for a short‑lived, taken‑down phishing campaign — and its silence is not exoneration of the ad platform, it is the archive's blind spot.
- **What it does record, and how it is misread.** Field 14 is a **fuzzy per‑creative search key, not a verified advertiser domain and not the click destination.** Proven three independent ways in this data: a `trezor.io` search returns `CR01860552808692973569`, whose PNG renders as a **Bybit `www.bybit.eu`** ad; a `ledger.com` search returns TCMMO's creative, which renders as a **Blueprint `www.blueprint.ai`** therapist‑software ad; a `coinbase.com` search returns HOP THANH's creative, which renders as a **Binance** ad. Add the negative control set (`MV_CTRL.json`): non‑crypto brand domains show the identical long tail of unrelated one‑creative advertisers — `veed.io` US 7 advertisers, `zazzle.com` DE 18, `ohora.com` US 22, `naver.com` KR 89. **"A mismatched company appears under a brand's domain" is the ATC baseline, not a compromise signal.** Any finding must come from downloading the `tpc.googlesyndication.com/archive/simgad/<id>` render and reading it; grepping the JSON for brand names produces both false all‑clears and false accusations.

Corollary for the postmortem: name **no** advertiser as the Trezor phisher — ATC cannot support it. The only publishable account‑integrity finding is `AR13216877914810744833` (Norm Reeves), framed as an unauthorised intrusion into a real dealership's live account running Binance brand‑bidding and cloaked display, Sept 2025, unconnected to this incident.
